chapters.meaning: What changed: the dollar gave back the rest of Monday's gain — DXY fell 0.40% Tuesday to ~102.1-102.2, extending the morning's fade (Asian session ~102.4). The driver was the Fed chorus, not data: Waller said the surge in long yields is doing some of the Fed's tightening work, favoring a hold in October; Williams reaffirmed one more hike in 2026 but said he sees no need for a hike in 2027; Collins backed another hike before year-end; Goolsbee warned AI-boom inflation is "jumping out of its lane." The market heard the doves more than the hawks. Data: existing home sales +1.5% m/m to 3.99m (vs -0.3% expected) — a beat that limited the damage; NFIB small-business optimism slipped 0.8 to 97.9, below its 52-year average, with inflation named the top problem by 20% of owners (up 4pts). Bank earnings: Goldman beat big ($17.01 vs $13.09 expected), Citi and Wells beat, JPM missed ($5.57 vs $5.90); Dimon warned on deficits, sticky inflation, elevated asset prices, rising rates, geopolitics. IMF lifted 2026 global growth to 3.1% (from 3.0%), US 2.3%. Thread: the hawkish hold is in week five; Monday the war bid and rate bid stacked into the 18-month top; the morning edition had the top stalling as the war premium leaked. What it means: confirms the stall, deepens it — now the rate leg wobbled too, not just the war leg. But the shape is unchanged: Dec ~85%, Oct ~19-22%. The thesis isn't broken; it's being repriced from "how many hikes" to "one and done."
numbers: Home sales +1.5% m/m to 3.99m vs -0.3% exp; NFIB 97.9 (-0.8)

scenarios.base: DXY chops 101.5-102.5 into CPI; the top holds as a ceiling while Dec stays ~85%.
scenarios.bear: Soft core (0.2% or below) collapses hike odds; crowded $35.5bn dollar longs squeeze and DXY gives back a percent.
scenarios.bull: Hot core (0.3%+) revives the October hike — DXY breaks out above the 1.5-year high.
